params.body:
The owner's YubiKey can now sign a working set or a widening of the gateway's policy from the Android app, held to the phone over NFC. Portal prepares the payload to sign and checks what comes back; it holds no operator key and never sees the PIN.

## Routes (owner session, `X-Portal-App: 1`)

- `GET /app/sign`: the operator keys the DID document publishes, the working set that stands, the projects, the policy draft that waits for the owner (`PolicyLog::waiting`, so not a narrowing), and the last eight steps of the trail.
- `POST /app/sign/offer`: a working set (projects, B1 or B2, one to seven days) or the waiting policy draft, as the payload to sign **without `iss`**. The app adds `iss` once it has read which operator key the YubiKey holds. An offer stands ten minutes and is used once (cache).
- `POST /app/sign/submit`: kept only when the signed claims, minus `iss`, are the offer exactly (compared as RFC 8785 bytes), `iss` is an operator key, and the signature holds. Then it goes through the door the laptop's signature uses: `WorkingSet::keep` or `PolicyLog::keep`. Refusals are named: `offer_lapsed`, `not_what_was_offered`, `not_an_operator_key`, `not_kept`, `nothing_waits`.
- `POST /app/sign/report`: what went wrong on the phone, as a name from a fixed list (wrong PIN, wrong key, slot without touch, NFC off, cancelled, ...). Free text cannot reach the trail this way.

## Audit trail

`signing_events` (new table, `SigningEvent`) records every step: offered, kept, refused with its reason, failed, cancelled. Each row has the issuer once it is known, the door it came through (`app`, `laptop`, `elixir`), the session's owner and the address. It never holds a PIN, a key or a token. The laptop's working-set door and the policy door write the same trail. To do that, the keeping logic moved from `IngestController::workingSet` to `WorkingSet::keep`, unchanged in behaviour.

## Gateway

No change. A policy version signed on the phone is the same token, by the same operator key, checked against the DID document. The gateway can't tell from an Ed25519 signature that the slot asked for a touch. Proposed as a separate decision in portal-android `docs/yubikey.md`: publish a PIV attestation per operator key, and refuse a key whose attestation doesn't show touch and PIN always.

## Tests

`tests/Feature/AppSignOnKeyTest.php` (8 tests) uses a software Ed25519 key in place of the YubiKey. It covers the door, the state, a working set kept once and its trail, every way a token differs from the offer (wider layer, an extra project, a forged signature, a hand's key, a lapsed offer), the bounds of an offer, and a policy version kept on the chain. That last test checks the exact signed bytes, and the app's test holds the same vector. The full suite passes except `BuildStampTest`, which reads `.git` and can't run in a git worktree.

The app side is the companion pull request in abovebeyond-ai/portal-android (`workbench/yubikey-nfc`).
params.title: Sign on the YubiKey from the app: offer, check, keep, and a trail
